name: Parmesan Garlic Sheet-Pan Chicken Thighs and Potatoes
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Source lists 723 cal / 31g protein using 6 bone-in skin-on thighs - clears both bars outright, all ingredients mapped, and it is a complete plate (protein, starch, vegetable) on one pan. The single best fit for the 'sheet-pan thigh dinner' gap. Confidence high; the write-up should trim the mayo-butter load a bit to bring calories toward 600. | HARVEST:
intro_html: This is the whole plate on one pan. Potatoes on the bottom soaking up drippings, green beans tucked around the edges, and chicken thighs under a garlic parmesan coat that browns into something close to a crust. No side dish to plan, no second pot to wash. Each container comes in at {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein for about ${{cost_ps}} (at everyday cost).
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 3 lb (1400 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh, 3 lb: ~$9.94. Buy 4 lbs: $12.88.
Lemon Juice, 0.7 lemons worth: ~$0.08. Buy 1 (lasts several batches).
Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper, italian seasoning, paprika): ~$0.36. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $20.59 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.47 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $28.47 across 14 servings, roughly $2.03 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $15.62 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $44.09. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for chicken, potatoes and green beans that all came off the same pan. Potatoes and green beans are the two cheapest things in the produce department, and this recipe leans on both of them hard.
shop_smart: Buy potatoes in the big bag, not loose. The per-pound price on a five or ten pound bag is usually half of what the loose bin charges, and potatoes keep for weeks somewhere cool and dark.

Frozen green beans beat fresh here on both price and behavior. They go straight from the freezer to the pan, they do not go slimy in the crisper drawer waiting on you, and the store brand bags are the cheapest vegetable per serving in this recipe.
Buy the tub of grated parmesan rather than a wedge. This recipe uses a few ounces and the tub keeps in the fridge for months, so you get several batches out of one purchase.

Mayonnaise is the secret to the coating, not a garnish. It keeps the parmesan glued to the chicken and the meat from drying out, and a jar you already have on the door costs you almost nothing per batch.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 425F. Cut the potatoes into bite-size chunks, toss them with most of the olive oil, salt, black pepper and paprika, and spread them across two large sheet pans in a single layer.
Roast the potatoes alone for 20 minutes, until the edges are starting to color. They need the head start; the chicken does not.
While they roast, stir together the melted butter, mayonnaise, minced garlic, grated parmesan, lemon juice and italian seasoning into a thick paste.
Pat the chicken thighs dry and coat every piece in the parmesan garlic mixture, front and back.
Pull the pans, push the potatoes to the edges, and nestle the coated thighs into the middle with the green beans scattered around them.
Roast another 20 to 25 minutes, until the chicken reads 165F, the coating is browned and blistered in spots, and the potatoes are crisp underneath.
Chop the chicken into pieces, scrape everything into your mixing pot with the pan drippings, and toss so the garlic butter coats the potatoes and beans too.
portion_html: Set the full pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight, and divide by 14. That number goes into every container, no more and no less. Each one lands at {{cal}} calories, and the potatoes hold their texture on reheat far better than rice does.

recipeIngredient: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh, 3 lb (1400 g)
steps: Toss cubed potatoes with olive oil, salt, pepper and paprika and roast at 425F for 20 minutes.
Mix melted butter, mayonnaise, garlic, parmesan, lemon juice and italian seasoning into a paste and coat the chicken thighs.
Add the coated thighs and the green beans to the potato pans.
Roast 20 to 25 minutes more until the chicken reads 165F and the coating browns.
Chop the chicken, toss everything with the pan drippings, and portion into 14 containers.
